Best For: Broad discovery, citation tracking, and setting up research alerts. Start here for any literature review.
WUB Access: ✅ Free (no account needed for basic use)
Notes:
Best first-stop for any research.
Use with advanced search operators (quotes, OR, date ranges).
Set up email alerts for key search terms.
Export citations to Zotero/Mendeley.
Weakness: struggles with niche keyword combinations — use specialized databases for focused searches.

Best For: Technical papers, engineering research, computing methodology, and hardware-adjacent research.
Notes:
Essential for engineering and computing research.
Use university email for full-text access.
Conference proceedings are often more current than journals for fast-moving fields.
Use 'Citation History' to track landmark papers.
Personal account saves searches and creates alerts.

Coverage: Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering
Best For: Core computing and software research. Covers algorithms, AI, data science, HCI, programming languages, and software engineering.
Notes:
ACM has two tiers: OA papers (free) + subscription content.
Many authors post preprints on arXiv or personal sites.
ACM Computing Surveys publishes excellent review papers across many domains.
Use ACM Classification System (CCS) for precise filtering.
If paywalled, try Unpaywall or contact authors via ResearchGate.

Coverage: All disciplines (Science, Tech, Medicine, Social Sciences)
Best For: Citation tracking, finding high-impact papers, systematic literature reviews, and bibliometric analysis.
Notes:
Confirmed accessible via WUB Library!
Use campus network/IP to access.
Scopus has superior citation data vs Google Scholar — 28K+ active journals.
Use 'Analyze Search Results' to see publication trends by year — great for identifying if a research topic is growing or declining.
Also useful for finding journal impact metrics.

Coverage: All disciplines (Science, Social Sciences, Arts & Humanities)
Best For: Finding high-impact journal papers, journal citation metrics (JCR), unique coverage in social sciences & humanities.
Notes:
Lower priority since Scopus is available.
WoS and Scopus overlap ~70% in journal coverage.
Use WoS specifically for: (1) Journal Citation Reports (JCR) impact factors, (2) Systematic reviews needing both databases, (3) Arts/humanities coverage.
Alternative: access individual papers via author preprints or Unpaywall.

Best For: Peer-reviewed STEM journal articles. Strong coverage across engineering, natural sciences, and social sciences.
WUB Access: ❓ Not directly confirmed via WUB Library
Notes:
Use university email for best access.
If paywalled, check for: (1) arXiv preprint, (2) author's ResearchGate profile, (3) Unpaywall extension.
Since Scopus (also Elsevier) is widely available, some Elsevier access may exist through institutional subscriptions — check with your librarian.

Coverage: Science, Technology, Medicine, Mathematics, Social Sciences
Best For: Books, major conference proceedings, and peer-reviewed journals across science and technology fields.
Notes:
Confirmed accessible via WUB Library!
Springer's LNCS (Lecture Notes in CS) series is a major source for computing conference proceedings.
Use advanced search filters by discipline, date, and content type.
Also check Springer's open access options (CC-licensed articles).

Best For: Education research, social science methodology, historical literature, and organizational studies.
Notes:
JSTOR offers JPASS — 100 free article views/month with personal account (no institutional login needed).
Useful for social sciences, humanities, and education research.
Also has research methodology guides.

Best For: Free preprints of the latest research. Essential for staying current in fast-moving research fields across STEM.
Notes:
Essential free resource!
Search by arXiv subject areas (e.g., cs, math, physics, stat).
Set up 'New submissions' email alerts for specific categories.
Warning: Preprints are NOT peer-reviewed — always verify if the work was later published in a peer-reviewed venue.
Use arxiv-vanity.com for better PDF reading.

Best For: Getting free PDFs of paywalled papers by requesting directly from authors. Following researchers and discovering related work.
Notes:
Best backup for paywalled papers.
Use 'Request full-text' to email the author directly.
Response rate ~60-70% within a few days.
Also useful for following researchers and seeing citation networks.

Coverage: Social Sciences, Economics, Law, Business, Humanities
Best For: Early research drafts and preprints in social sciences, economics, and law. Good for finding working papers before formal publication.
Notes:
Owned by Elsevier but remains free to read.
Good for: economics, labor studies, education policy, and legal research.
Many international organizations (World Bank, IMF) and researchers post working papers here before journal publication.
Use 'Top Papers' rankings to find influential working papers.

Best For: Biomedical literature, health sciences, and life science research papers.
Notes:
PubMed (citations) is free; PMC (PubMed Central) provides free full-text access.
WUB Library has PubMed as a quick-link resource.
Tip: PMC's full-text corpus is available for text mining (PMC Open Access Subset).
Essential for biomedical and health-related research.

Best For: Sourcing open-access papers completely free. Finding content from institutional repositories, theses, and dissertations.
Notes:
World's largest open-access aggregator — harvests content from 10K+ repositories.
Use when: you find a paywalled paper, check CORE for OA version.
Also excellent for finding theses and dissertations.
Has a free API for programmatic access.

Best For: AI-powered semantic paper matching, TLDR summaries, and citation graph visualization. Excellent for discovering related research.
Notes:
Built by Allen Institute for AI.
Key features: TLDR AI-generated summaries, 'Highly Influential Citations' filter, semantic graph visualization.
Use the API for programmatic search and 'Research Feeds' for personalized paper recommendations.
Particularly strong in computing and AI fields.

Best For: Building visual web graphs of connected research. Discovering papers that cite or are cited by the same sources as a known paper.
Notes:
Great for literature review expansion.
Start with one key paper → graph of related work.
Uses co-citation + bibliographic coupling.
Free tier: ~5 graphs/month.
Use early in literature review to map research landscape.

Best For: AI-powered extraction of methodology, results, and findings across multiple papers. Ask research questions and get structured answers.
Notes:
Use for efficient literature review.
Instead of reading 20 papers manually, ask Elicit to extract columns (method, sample size, findings) across papers.
Free tier limited (~5-10 searches/month).
Best for: comparing methodologies across multiple papers systematically.

Best For: Getting research-backed answers to plain questions. Quickly checking if there's scientific consensus on a topic.
Notes:
Quickest way to check research-backed claims.
Ask question → get answer synthesized from multiple papers with citations.
Free tier functional for basic queries.
Best for: checking assumptions, finding papers on specific relationships, quick literature overview.

Best For: Global workforce trends, job market projections, and analysis of how technology and AI are reshaping employment. Published annually.
Notes:
Published annually — each edition covers job growth projections through the next 3-5 years.
Useful for identifying emerging job categories, tracking automation/AI displacement trends, and understanding global skill shifts.
Download full PDF for valuable data tables in appendices.

Coverage: US tech workforce, global IT trends
Best For: Technology workforce analysis and hiring reports. US tech employment data, skill demand trends, and employer benchmarks.
Notes:
'State of the Tech Workforce' is the go-to source for US tech employment numbers, hiring projections, and skill demand rankings.
Also publishes role-specific reports (Cybersecurity, Cloud, AI).
Tech Town Index rates US metropolitan areas for tech jobs.

Best For: Largest annual survey of software developers worldwide. Covers programming languages, tools, frameworks, salaries, and developer demographics.
Notes:
Raw CSV data is publicly downloadable — researchers can run their own analysis.
Covers: programming languages, frameworks, tools, salary by country, education levels, experience.
The 'Technology' section ranks technologies by usage percentage.
Useful for validating technology adoption trends.

Best For: Country-level programming proficiency rankings, skill benchmarks, and hiring assessment trends.
Notes:
'Developer Skills Report' ranks countries by programming proficiency.
Shows which skills are tested most in hiring assessments (SQL, Problem Solving, Python).
Data biased toward HackerRank users — use for supplementary context only.

Coverage: Global IT and professional certification data
Best For: Global IT and professional certification trends. Exam volume data, certification popularity, testing trends.
Notes:
Pearson VUE publishes annual 'Testing Trends' reports showing exam volumes for major certifications (CompTIA, Cisco, Microsoft, AWS).
Useful for understanding which certifications are growing in demand.
Data shows certification trends by region.

Best For: Skills pay premiums and salary market benchmarks. Data on which skills command higher compensation.
Notes:
Publishes quarterly 'IT Skills & Certifications Pay Index' — tracks which skills earn salary premiums.
Most detailed data behind paywall.
US/North America focused.
Use free summaries for supplementary context.

Coverage: US labor market (formerly Emsi Burning Glass)
Best For: Detailed structural labor market records. Real-time job posting data, skill demand analytics, employer requirement shifts.
Notes:
Gold standard for labor market analytics — analyzes millions of job postings.
Free reports + blog posts are valuable.
Skill Infrastructure taxonomy is a useful reference for standardizing skill names in any labor-related research.

Best For: Real-time tracking of employer requirement shifts. Job posting analytics and skill trend data.
Notes:
Acquired by Lightcast (2021) — same company.
Research arm still publishes under both brands.
Focus on Lightcast for current data; Burning Glass archives for historical trend analysis (pre-2021).

Best For: Broad socio-economic development datasets. Education, employment, and labor market data for developing countries worldwide.
Notes:
World Development Indicators database includes education, employment, and ICT-related metrics.
'Skills for Employability' program has country-specific reports.
Use data.worldbank.org for quick statistical queries.
Extensive education and employment data across 250+ economies.

Best For: Global labor statistics, employment rates, working conditions, and international labor standards.
Notes:
ILOSTAT database has country-level employment data by sector.
ISCO-08 classification is an ILO standard — useful for occupational classification in any labor research.
'World Employment and Social Outlook' reports provide authoritative global labor data.
Country-specific publications available.

Best For: Regional development reports, labor market analysis, education-to-employment studies, and skill gap reports for Asia-Pacific countries.
Notes:
Publishes extensive labor market and development reports for Asia-Pacific countries.
'Asian Development Outlook' includes country-by-country chapters.
'Skills Development' program reports are useful for education-to-employment research in developing Asia.

Best For: The computer science bibliography. Finding CS conference and journal papers by venue, author, or year.
Notes:
Essential for computer science research.
Covers all major CS conferences and journals.
Use for: finding papers by specific venue, tracking authors, checking publication dates.
Free and open — no login needed.
Has a search API for programmatic queries.

Best For: Free, open index of research works with programmatic API access. Successor to Microsoft Academic Graph.
Notes:
Successor to Microsoft Academic Graph.
Has a REST API for programmatic literature queries — useful for bibliometric analysis, trend identification, and cross-referencing research topics.
Entire dataset available for bulk download.
Much more powerful than Google Scholar for programmatic access.

Best For: Finding peer-reviewed open access journals. Sourcing freely accessible papers when institutional access fails.
Notes:
Directory of Open Access Journals — 20K+ journals, all fully free.
Use when: you hit a paywalled paper and need an OA alternative.
Filter by subject, publisher, license type.
Good for finding legitimate OA journals for potential publication.

Best For: Browser extension that automatically finds free OA versions of paywalled papers when browsing.
Notes:
Install in your browser.
When you land on a paywalled paper page, Unpaywall automatically searches repositories for a free OA version.
Works with Chrome, Firefox, Edge.
Green/gold icon indicates OA availability.
Sources from 100K+ repositories worldwide.

Best For: Latest research before formal publication. Open peer review platform with public discussion and commentary.
Notes:
Papers posted here often months before conference acceptance.
Public peer review discussions provide insights into paper strengths and weaknesses.
Good for tracking cutting-edge developments in AI, ML, and related fields.

Best For: Open data and paper repository by CERN. Finding datasets, supplementary materials, and research software.
Notes:
Created by CERN.
Researchers upload datasets, code, and supplementary materials alongside their papers.
Useful for finding: pre-trained models, annotated datasets, and code repositories.
Also good for archiving your own research data (each upload gets a DOI).
Has a REST API.

Best For: Public datasets for ML and data science projects. Notebooks with free GPU. Competitions for benchmarking models.
Notes:
50K+ public datasets across many domains.
Free GPU for notebooks (alternative to Colab).
Also has learning courses and community discussions.
Useful for finding datasets relevant to your research domain.

Best For: Education research database. Finding papers on curriculum design, educational technology, and learning outcomes.
Notes:
Sponsored by the U.S. Department of Education's Institute of Education Sciences.
The premier database for education-related research.
Useful for finding studies on educational technology, online learning effectiveness, curriculum design, and education-to-employment research.
Includes journal articles, conference papers, reports, and policy documents.

Best For: Global skills policy data, education indicators, and international employment statistics.
Notes:
OECD Skills Outlook and Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) are highly regarded for international skills comparison.
OECD iLibrary has extensive reports on education, employment, and social policy.
Free data portal (data-explorer.oecd.org) for statistical queries.

Best For: Monthly workforce reports on hiring rates, talent migration, and skill trends by country and industry.
Notes:
LinkedIn publishes monthly workforce reports covering hiring rates by industry, top growing skills, and talent migration patterns.
Their 'Skills Graph' data maps relationships between skills and demand trends.
LinkedIn Talent Insights (paid) offers deeper analytics.
Free reports useful for cross-country validation.

Coverage: Global (US, UK, Canada, Australia, Germany, France)
Best For: Data-driven reports on wage trends, employer demand, and labor market conditions based on millions of job postings.
Notes:
Indeed's research arm publishes reports based on their global job posting database.
Topics include: employer demand trends, salary tracking, remote work impact, and skill requirements evolution.
Free blog posts and PDF reports available.

Best For: Skill proficiency rankings by country across business, technology, and data science domains.
Notes:
Annual report ranking 100+ countries on skill proficiency in technology, data science, and business domains.
Published annually as a free PDF download.
Useful for cross-country skill benchmarking and understanding regional strengths and weaknesses.

Best For: Bangladesh Association of Software and Information Services. Local IT industry data, employment surveys, and skill gap reports.
Notes:
National trade body for Bangladesh's IT industry.
Publishes member surveys on skill gaps, IT export data, workforce statistics, and industry event reports.
Useful for researchers focusing on Bangladesh's IT sector.
Also organizes job fairs — provides insight into local hiring landscape.

Best For: Government ICT policy documents, national digital strategy, skill development programs, and IT workforce data for Bangladesh.
Notes:
Bangladesh government's ICT Division publishes National ICT Policy, Digital Bangladesh strategy, skill development program reports, and IT park data.
Important for understanding government perspectives on IT skills and employment.
Also check a2i (a2i.gov.bd) for innovation program reports.

Best For: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics. National labor force surveys, wage surveys, education statistics, and employment data by sector.
Notes:
Primary source for Bangladesh-specific labor metrics.
Publishes: Labor Force Survey (annual), Wage Employment Survey, Education Household Survey.
Useful for researchers working on Bangladesh labor market or education topics.
Data available in PDF reports and some Excel tables.

Best For: IT market research, technology trend analysis, and industry forecasts. Widely cited in both academic and industry publications.
Notes:
Widely cited in industry and academic publications.
Gartner Hype Cycle tracks technology maturity cycles.
Top Skills reports predict future technology demand.
Detailed reports are behind paywall (~$1K+), but free summaries and press releases contain usable insights.

Best For: US Bureau of Labor Statistics. Occupational outlook, wage data, employment projections, and the O*NET database.
Notes:
O*NET database (onetonline.org) comes from BLS — provides detailed occupational classifications, skill definitions, and wage data.
Useful for research involving US labor market or as a reference for occupational taxonomy.
Data downloadable in bulk.

Best For: Global education statistics, ICT in education reports, and technical/vocational education and training (TVET) studies.
Notes:
UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) provides education data by country.
Useful for global education benchmarks and understanding education-to-employment pathways.
'Global Education Monitoring Report' covers skills and education policy.
Country-specific reports available.
